bolted.tightening_torque.title: Bolt preload from tightening torque (T = K·F·d)

variables.name: K
variables.desc: nut factor (0.2 typical dry steel, lubricated ~0.15)

assumptions: T = K·F_i·d relates torque to preload through the nut factor K (a user input that depends on thread friction and finish); scatter of ±25 % is common. For a reliable preload use torque-angle or direct tensioning.
method_references: T = K F d (short-form torque–preload relation, recalled)

bolted.tensile_stress_area.title: Bolt tensile stress area (ISO metric)
assumptions: ISO metric (coarse and fine): At = π/4 (d − 0.9382 p)², the area of the mean of the pitch and minor diameters. Unified (UN) threads use At = 0.7854 (d − 0.9743/n)² with d in inches and n threads/in — not computed here.
method_references: ISO metric tensile stress area At = π/4 (d − 0.9382 p)² (recalled)

bolted.bolt_stiffness.title: Bolt stiffness (threaded + unthreaded portions)
assumptions: Two springs in series (threaded and unthreaded shank): 1/k_b = L_d/(A_d E) + L_t/(A_t E). Head and nut flexibility are neglected.
method_references: Bolt stiffness k_b = A_d A_t E / (A_d L_t + A_t L_d) (Shigley form, recalled)

bolted.member_stiffness_frustum.title: Member stiffness (Shigley 30° cone frustum)

procedure.python:
def _frustum(values):
    """Member stiffness of a joint with two equal clamped members (equal-member two-frustum form).

    One frustum grows from the head and one from the nut, each of length L/2, in series (hence the
    factor 2 in the denominator):

    k_m = π E d tanα / (2 ln[ ((L tanα + D − d)(D + d)) / ((L tanα + D + d)(D − d)) ])

    with D the washer/head face diameter, α the cone half-apex angle (≈30°), d the bolt diameter and
    L the total grip length.
    """
    E, d, D, alpha, L = values['E'], values['d'], values['D'], values['alpha'], values['L']
    if D <= d:
        raise MechError('member_stiffness_frustum: washer face diameter D must exceed the bolt diameter d')
    t = math.tan(alpha)
    if L * t + D - d <= 0:
        raise MechError('member_stiffness_frustum: L·tan(alpha) + D − d must be positive')
    arg = ((L * t + D - d) * (D + d)) / ((L * t + D + d) * (D - d))
    den = 2.0 * math.log(arg)
    if den <= 0:
        raise MechError('member_stiffness_frustum: frustum geometry gives a non-positive stiffness')
    return {'k_m': PI * E * d * t / den}

assumptions: Axisymmetric frustum, one from the head and one from the nut (two equal clamped members, L/2 each, in series) with half-apex angle α (≈30° for steel). Requires D > d. Valid while the frusta do not overlap the full grip.
method_references: Shigley frustum member stiffness (closed form, recalled)

bolted.member_stiffness_wileman.title: Member stiffness (Wileman exponential)
assumptions: Wileman–Choudury–Green empirical member stiffness k_m = E·d·A·exp(B·d/L); A and B are tabulated (material and aspect ratio) user inputs.

bolted.joint_constant.title: Joint constant (C = kb/(kb + km))

variables.name: C
variables.desc: joint constant (fraction of the external load carried by the bolt)

assumptions: C is the fraction of an external tensile load that adds to the bolt; (1 − C) unloads the member. Soft members (small k_m) give a large C.

bolted.preload.title: Preload from proof strength, and load/separation factors

variables.name: k
variables.desc: preload as a fraction of proof load (≈0.75 reusable, ≈0.9 permanent)

variables.name: n_L
variables.desc: load factor (margin to proof strength under external load)

variables.name: n_sep
variables.desc: factor of safety against joint separation

assumptions: Preload as a fraction k of the proof load Sp·A_t (k ≈ 0.75 for reusable joints, ≈ 0.9 for permanent joints — guidance, not a built-in value). The load factor n_L = (Sp A_t − F_i)/(C P) is the factor by which the external load could grow before the bolt reaches proof strength; n_sep = F_i/((1−C) P) guards separation.
method_references: Preload F_i = k A_t Sp and the load/separation factors (recalled)

bolted.load_sharing.title: External-load sharing and separation load

variables.name: F_b
variables.desc: bolt load under external load P

variables.name: F_m
variables.desc: member load under external load P

variables.name: P_sep
variables.desc: external load that just separates the joint

procedure.python:
def _load_sharing(values):
    """External-load sharing, separation load and a separation warning for a preloaded joint.

    C = k_b/(k_b + k_m); the bolt carries F_i + C P and the member F_i − (1−C) P. When P exceeds
    P_sep = F_i/(1−C) the member load reaches zero — the joint separates and the bolt carries the
    full external load — which is surfaced as a warning.
    """
    kb, km, Fi, P = values['k_b'], values['k_m'], values['F_i'], values['P']
    if kb <= 0 or km <= 0:
        raise MechError('load_sharing: bolt and member stiffness must be positive')
    if Fi < 0 or P < 0:
        raise MechError('load_sharing: preload and external load must be non-negative')
    C = kb / (kb + km)
    F_b = Fi + C * P
    F_m = Fi - (1.0 - C) * P
    P_sep = Fi / (1.0 - C)
    out = {'F_b': F_b, 'F_m': F_m, 'C': C, 'P_sep': P_sep}
    if P > P_sep:
        out['_warnings'] = ['load_sharing: P exceeds P_sep — the joint has separated (F_m <= 0) and '
                            'the bolt carries the full external load P']
    return out

assumptions: Linear elastic bolt and member. The joint separates (loses clamp) when the member load reaches zero, at P = F_i/(1 − C); a warning is raised when P > P_sep (the member load F_m goes negative and the bolt carries the full external load).
method_references: Bolt/member load sharing: F_b = F_i + C P, F_m = F_i − (1−C) P

bolted.bolt_fatigue.title: Bolt fatigue safety factor (Goodman) and separation

variables.name: n_fatigue
variables.desc: Goodman factor of safety on the bolt

variables.name: n_sep
variables.desc: factor of safety against joint separation

procedure.python:
def _bolt_fatigue(values):
    """Bolt fatigue by the constant-preload Goodman line, plus the separation factor of safety.

    The bolt stress oscillates between σi = F_i/A_t and σi + C·Pmax/A_t, so the alternating stress is
    σa = C(Pmax − Pmin)/(2 A_t) and the midrange stress is σm = C(Pmax + Pmin)/(2 A_t) + σi. With the
    Goodman line drawn from the preload (the preload is always present), the factor of safety is
    n_f = Se(Sut − σi) / (Sut σa + Se(σm − σi)).
    """
    Fi, C, Pmax, Pmin, At, Se, Sut = (values[k] for k in ('F_i', 'C', 'Pmax', 'Pmin', 'A_t', 'Se', 'Sut'))
    if Pmax < Pmin:
        raise MechError('bolt_fatigue: Pmax must be >= Pmin')
    if not (0.0 < C < 1.0):
        raise MechError('bolt_fatigue: the joint constant C must lie between 0 and 1')
    if Pmax <= 0:
        raise MechError('bolt_fatigue: Pmax must be positive')
    if At <= 0 or Se <= 0 or Sut <= 0:
        raise MechError('bolt_fatigue: A_t, Se and Sut must be positive')
    sigma_i = Fi / At
    sigma_a = C * (Pmax - Pmin) / (2.0 * At)
    sigma_m = C * (Pmax + Pmin) / (2.0 * At) + sigma_i
    n_sep = Fi / ((1.0 - C) * Pmax)   # separation when F_m = F_i − (1−C)·Pmax reaches zero
    out = {'sigma_a': sigma_a, 'sigma_m': sigma_m, 'n_sep': n_sep}
    if Pmax == Pmin:
        # static (no alternating) load: the fatigue factor of safety is undefined
        out['n_fatigue'] = None
        out['_warnings'] = ['bolt_fatigue: Pmin == Pmax (static load, σa = 0) — the fatigue factor of '
                            'safety is undefined; use a static strength check instead']
    else:
        out['n_fatigue'] = Se * (Sut - sigma_i) / (Sut * sigma_a + Se * (sigma_m - sigma_i))
    return out

assumptions: External load fluctuates between Pmin and Pmax; the bolt sees C·P of it. σi = F_i/A_t; σa = C·(Pmax−Pmin)/(2 A_t); σm = C·(Pmax+Pmin)/(2 A_t) + σi. The constant-preload Goodman form n_f = Se(Sut−σi)/(Sut σa + Se(σm−σi)) is used (the preload is always present). Separation is guarded by n_sep = F_i/((1−C)·Pmax). Pmin = Pmax (static) gives n_fatigue = null with a note.
method_references: Bolt fatigue with constant preload and joint separation (recalled)

bolted.thread_stripping.title: Thread stripping area and shear stress

variables.name: f
variables.desc: engaged-fraction of thread in shear (coarse user input, ≈0.5)

assumptions: Simple cylinder model of the external-thread shear area: A = π·d_min·L_e·f with f a coarse engaged-fraction user input (≈0.5). A refined treatment balances the internal (nut) and external (bolt) thread shear areas; their diameter ratio w_i/w_o ≈ 0.75–0.88 sets the equal-strength nut. Exact ASME B1.1 / ISO 898 formulas give precise stripping areas.

bolted.bolt_group_eccentric.title: Bolt group in shear with eccentric loading (elastic method)

variables.name: x_p
variables.desc: x of the load application point

variables.name: y_p
variables.desc: y of the load application point

variables.name: moment
variables.desc: eccentric moment about the bolt centroid

procedure.python:
def _bolt_group(values):
    """Elastic (torsion) analysis of a bolt group under an eccentric shear load.

    Direct shear is shared equally; the moment M about the bolt centroid is resisted by shear
    proportional to each bolt's distance from the centroid (elastic method, no instantaneous-centre
    iteration). Returns per-bolt resultants and the largest one.
    """
    bolts = values['bolts']
    if not isinstance(bolts, list) or len(bolts) < 2:
        raise MechError('bolt_group_eccentric: need at least two bolt coordinates [[x, y], ...]')
    n = len(bolts)
    pts = []
    for row in bolts:
        if len(row) != 2:
            raise MechError('bolt_group_eccentric: each bolt must be [x_m, y_m]')
        pts.append((float(row[0]), float(row[1])))
    Fx, Fy = values['F_x'], values['F_y']
    xp, yp = values['x_p'], values['y_p']
    xc = sum(x for x, _ in pts) / n
    yc = sum(y for _, y in pts) / n
    M = (xp - xc) * Fy - (yp - yc) * Fx        # CCW positive, r × F
    sumr2 = sum((x - xc) ** 2 + (y - yc) ** 2 for x, y in pts)
    if sumr2 <= 0:
        raise MechError('bolt_group_eccentric: all bolts coincide with the centroid')
    dx, dy = Fx / n, Fy / n
    rows, max_shear = [], 0.0
    for x, y in pts:
        rx, ry = x - xc, y - yc
        ftx = -M * ry / sumr2
        fty = M * rx / sumr2
        bx, by = dx + ftx, dy + fty
        f = math.hypot(bx, by)
        max_shear = max(max_shear, f)
        rows.append([bx, by, f])
    return {'moment': M, 'direct_x': dx, 'direct_y': dy, 'max_shear': max_shear, 'bolt_forces': rows}

assumptions: Elastic (torsion) method: equal direct shear F/n plus torsional shear proportional to distance from the centroid (no instantaneous-centre plastic iteration). The eccentric moment is M = (x_p−x̄)F_y − (y_p−ȳ)F_x.
method_references: Elastic analysis of an eccentrically loaded bolt group (recalled)

bolted.rivet_shear.title: Rivet shear and bearing stress
assumptions: Average stresses: shear on m·n rivet cross-sections; bearing on the projected area n·d·t of the plate. Single shear m = 1, double (butt with cover plates) m = 2.
method_references: Rivet shear τ = F/(m·n·πd²/4); bearing σb = F/(n·d·t)

bolted.rivet_efficiency.title: Riveted joint strength and efficiency (per pitch)

variables.name: F_shear
variables.desc: joint strength in rivet shear (per pitch)

variables.name: F_tearing
variables.desc: joint strength in plate tearing (per pitch)

variables.name: F_solid
variables.desc: strength of the solid (unpierced) plate per pitch

assumptions: Per-pitch strengths with n rivets per pitch length p: shear m·n·πd²/4·τ_allow, bearing n·d·t·σb, tearing across the outer-row net section (p − d)·t·σt (one hole per pitch in the outer row), solid plate p·t·σt. The joint efficiency is η = min(F_shear, F_bearing, F_tearing)/F_solid. Requires p > d for a positive net section.
method_references: Riveted joint strengths and efficiency (standard forms, recalled)

source.derivation: Static load (Pmin = Pmax): σa = 0, so the fatigue factor of safety is undefined (null, with a note). σm = σi + C·Pmax/A_t = 237.248 + 0.1176·10000/84.3e-6 = 237.248 + 13.9502 = 251.198 MPa; n_sep = 2.26655

Two rivets per pitch in double shear: F_shear = n·m·(π d²/4)·τ = 2·2·78.5398e-6·100e6 = 31415.9 N; F_bearing = n·d·t·σb = 2·0.010·0.008·250e6 = 40000 N; F_tearing (outer row, one hole per pitch) = (p − d)·t·σt = 0.030·0.008·80e6 = 19200 N; F_solid = p·t·σt = 25600 N; η = min/solid = 19200/25600 = 0.75
